# Documents & sharing

The **Docs** drawer (sidebar folder icon) is the unified view of every file in your workspace.

## What's in it

- **Uploads** — anything you've dragged into chat or uploaded directly (PDFs, images, CSVs, code).
- **AI images** — every image generated by your image agent.
- **AI videos** — every video from the video generator.
- **Research documents** — long-form research output from `deep_research`.
- **Code projects** — sandboxed projects the coder has worked in. Downloadable as zip.
- **Notes** — a separate tab for free-form personal notes.

Tabs at the top of the drawer filter by kind (Documents / Images / Videos / Audio / Code).

## Select multiple files

Use the **Select** checkbox on each file, or **Select all in this tab**.
Your selection stays selected when you switch tabs, so you can include images,
videos, documents, audio, and code projects together. **Clear** removes the
whole selection.

- **Download selected** prepares one ZIP and saves it through your browser.
  It includes shared files you can access. Duplicate filenames are numbered;
  code projects appear as folders without dependencies or build output.
  Each ZIP supports up to 250 selected items, 10,000 files, and 5 GB.
- **Delete selected** asks for confirmation once, then removes your selected
  files permanently. Shared files belong to their original owner: deselect
  them before deleting. Admin status does not grant permission to delete
  another user's documents. Any failed deletions are reported and remaining
  files stay selected so you can retry.

Single-file previews, downloads, sharing, and agent actions remain on each card.

## Attach, keep, and reference files

Attach up to six files to one message using the paperclip, drag-and-drop, or
paste. Check the attachment tray before sending. The message keeps references
to all of its sent attachments across a reload.

When **Keep … in your files?** appears after a reply, **Keep** leaves the file
in your profile and **Discard** deletes the saved file. Ignoring that prompt
keeps it. Removing an unsent item from the tray is a separate action.

Type `@` to find an agent or a saved file. For example, choose
`@audio/meeting.wav` from autocomplete to reference an existing recording.

## Transcribe audio and video

Attach a recording and ask “Transcribe this,” or reference a saved audio/video
file with `@`. OE uses its configured [STT service](../stt/); video transcription
also needs ffmpeg to extract the audio. The upload limit is 500 MB, and the
chosen transcription provider can have a smaller input limit.

Uploaded audio appears under **Audio**, with an inline player. Earlier files
may remain in their original Documents location. Cloud transcription sends
the recording to that configured provider.

## Sharing with other users on the same install

Click the share icon on any item, pick which users to share it with, save. Shared files show up in the recipient's Docs drawer with an "uploaded by {name}" label. Sharing is one-way: the original owner can revoke; recipients can't reshare.

You can also share with **everyone** by setting the audience to "Everyone" — useful for house-wide reference docs.

## Sharing outside the install

OpenEnsemble doesn't generate public download URLs by default — sharing is intra-install. If you want a doc on the public internet, download it locally and host it elsewhere. This is deliberate: most installs aren't internet-facing.

## How agents use documents

The `profile_files` skill is the single tool every agent uses to list and read your files: *"Summarise the PDF I uploaded yesterday"* works because the agent can list and open everything in your Docs drawer. (Earlier versions had a separate `shared-docs` skill — that's been folded into `profile_files`. Cross-user shares show up annotated with the sharing user's name.)

Anything you drop into chat — paperclip, paste, drag — now persists with a stable `file_id` (e.g. `documents:doc_abc123`). Earlier versions kept chat uploads only for the immediate turn; they're now first-class files you can reference in later sessions, attach to email by id, or list via `list_profile_files`.

Agents can also *add* to your Docs drawer:
- Image agent → AI images tab
- Video agent → AI videos tab
- Researcher → Research tab
- Coder → Code Projects tab

## Editing documents with your agent

Text documents (markdown, txt, csv, code files) **and research documents** can be edited by asking your agent — there's no manual editor; chat is the interface:

1. Open the doc in the Docs drawer and hit the **🤖 Ask Agent** button (or just mention the doc in chat).
2. Tell the agent what to change: *"fix the grammar"*, *"make it more formal"*, *"add a section about pricing"*.
3. Chat shows a compact document preview while the agent works, then a clickable preview of the saved result. The document body is not dumped into the conversation.
4. Click the result to open the document workspace. The current document, version history, and review controls update live.

**Nothing is ever lost.** Every edit is saved as a new version — the original upload becomes v1 the first time a doc is edited, and every iteration after that is kept. The workspace keeps the full trail in the right-side **History** rail: who changed what and when, a side-by-side comparison with the preceding version, and one-click **Restore** (which itself adds a new version, so restores are undoable).

Agents can also create brand-new documents (*"make me a packing list for the camping trip"*) — they land in the Documents tab.

Only the document's **owner** can edit or restore; docs shared with you are read-only (ask your agent for an edited copy instead). PDFs, Word files, and media can't be edited — only viewed. Research documents get the same version trail whether you edit them from the viewer or the Researcher updates them itself.

## Network shares (SMB and NFS)

Connect a NAS or file server from **Settings → Network Shares**, or ask in chat:

- “Connect to the shared folder on shareserver.”
- “Connect to `//shareserver/shared`.”
- “Connect to `nfs://shareserver/export/data`.”
- “What's in that share?”
- “Read the project notes in it.”
- “Copy my report to `reports/report.pdf` on that share.”
- “Pull the photos into my OE Images folder.”

Connections belong to your signed-in OE account. Adult accounts with the
Network Shares skill enabled can use them. The share must be reachable from
the **OE server**. A share reachable only from your laptop needs network access
from OE too. Existing TV video-library sources remain household media sources;
connect a folder here to use it for your account's chat and file transfers.

If you know only the server name, OE can list its advertised SMB shares and
NFS exports. It asks which folder to use if the answer is ambiguous. Some NFSv4
servers do not advertise exports; an exact export address can still work.

For SMB, OE tries your saved login or guest access. When a login is required,
an inline form collects **Username**, **Password**, and optional **Domain**.
Submitting it continues the connection. These fields bypass the chat transcript
and model; a successful login is saved encrypted for your account. To replace
a saved login, ask to connect with a new login. Cancel closes the request
without saving a new connection. In Settings, enter the same fields directly.

NFS supports versions 3 and 4 and defaults to 4. Select the server's version in
Settings or mention it in chat. NFS uses the OE service's operating-system
UID/GID and the server's export permissions. It does not accept an SMB password.
The server must allow this host and identity. Exports that require a reserved
client port need an administrator to configure that access for `fuse-nfs`.
Kerberos-based NFS login is not configured by this feature.

Use **Browse** to inspect a saved share. Chat can list directories, read text,
extract PDF text, show small images, and copy files or folders in either
direction. Documents accepts regular files; Images, Videos, and Audio accept
their media type. Imported documents appear in Profile Files with their source
names and new file IDs. Media imports use unique filenames. Source files stay
in place. Copies do not overwrite existing files or follow symbolic links.
Each copy is limited to 2,000 files and 1 GiB; large directories can be copied
in smaller groups. A failed or interrupted upload may leave a partial destination;
OE reports failures instead of claiming the copy succeeded.

To remove particular files, ask for those files to be deleted **from** the share,
for example, “remove both daily news briefings from the share.” OE lists the
share to identify the exact filenames and deletes only the selected files.
The share stays connected, its saved settings remain, and any originals in OE
are preserved. File deletion supports up to 100 regular files per request;
it rejects folders, symbolic links, the share root, and wildcard patterns.

In chat, asking to remove the share itself presents three choices: **remove from OE
only**, keeping the server share and all files; **delete all files and the
share**; or **ignore this request**, keeping the connection, share, and files
unchanged. Reply **3**, **ignore this request**, or **cancel** to cancel removal.
Nothing changes until you choose. Permanent deletion requires an
administrator, an authorized server node, and a separate typed confirmation
that names the exact SMB or NFS address. A generic “yes” does not confirm
deletion. Choices expire after ten minutes and apply only in the same chat.

**Disconnect** unmounts the share, keeps its saved settings, and turns off
automatic mounting. **Forget** removes the OE connection and any saved login
unused by other shares on that server. Both preserve the server share and all
files. Opening or connecting a saved share again enables automatic mounting.

Connected shares **mount automatically 30 seconds after OE starts**, including
after a server reboot, using their saved encrypted login. If a server is
unavailable or a connection times out, OE retries after another 30, 60, 120,
and 240 seconds. These waits do not block OE startup. Disconnecting or
forgetting a share cancels its remaining retries. Rejected logins and other
configuration errors need attention instead of automatic retries.

Connection failures do not erase saved settings. Use **Connect** to try again
after the startup retries finish; a changed SMB login can be replaced in the
protected form. Backups contain connection settings and encrypted credentials,
not the remote share's contents.

### Host setup and troubleshooting

Network shares use Linux FUSE, rclone's SMB client, and fuse-nfs. On Debian,
Ubuntu, or Mint, `install.sh` installs the host prerequisites and prepares the
share clients automatically. Existing installations also install missing
clients on the first discovery or connection attempt. Concurrent requests wait
for the same installation. On a normal Linux host, the installer also loads the
FUSE kernel module if needed. Container hosts must grant device access outside
the guest.

Ask **“Check network-share support”** to check dependencies and mount/unmount a
temporary local test folder. This does not contact your NAS or read your files.
Settings → Network Shares also shows missing setup. FUSE failures are reported
separately from SMB login and NFS export errors.

An owner/admin can ask **“Set up network-share support”** to repair the local
installation. OE installs missing prerequisites, prepares clients, and runs the
mount test again. If sudo needs a password, enter it only in OE's protected
form. Ordinary account users can check support and ask an administrator to fix it.

For **Docker Compose or Proxmox LXC**, pair the Linux host as a node with full
access and give OE the exact container name/ID. OE verifies the running
container's identity before configuring it. Proxmox setup merges `fuse=1`
without discarding existing feature flags. Docker setup requires the original
Compose files, checks ports and mounts against the running container, pins its
current image and environment, verifies that OE's config/profiles/restart
checkpoint are on persistent volumes, and stages a private configuration on
the host. Edited Compose settings must be reconciled before automatic recreation.
It passes `/dev/fuse`, adds `SYS_ADMIN`, and uses an OE AppArmor policy restricted
to FUSE mounts in OE's temporary share directories where AppArmor is enabled.
Existing custom security policies and unsupported runtimes require their
administrator; OE does not disable those protections.

OE reports when the container needs restarting/recreating. A protected
**RESTART** confirmation saves the conversation and schedules that operation on
the host; OE checks support again when it returns. A prepared configuration is
not reported as a successful mount. Host receipts and the staged Docker config
are under `/var/lib/openensemble-share-setup/`; keep using the returned staged
Compose configuration when managing that deployment, or merge its FUSE settings
into the original Compose files. It contains the effective environment and is
readable only by root. Proxmox documents FUSE limitations with freezer-based
snapshot/suspend backups; use a compatible backup mode or host-mounted shares.

The client installer, `scripts/install-share-tools.sh`, downloads
architecture-matched packages and builds a pinned fuse-nfs client under OE's
ignored `bin/` directory. It preserves existing mounts and skips clients that
are already ready. An administrator can also re-run `install.sh` to repair host
prerequisites. Other Linux distributions can provide rclone, fuse-nfs, and
showmount on the service PATH.

For **access denied**, check the SMB login/domain or the NFS export's host and
UID/GID rules. For **unavailable**, check the address, firewall, and server.
For **destination exists**, choose another filename. NFS support and reserved
port setup are described in the [fuse-nfs documentation](https://github.com/sahlberg/fuse-nfs);
SMB options are documented by [rclone](https://rclone.org/smb/).

## Storage

Files live under `users/{userId}/`:
- `documents/` — profile files, including document and media folders
- `documents/code/` — code projects
- Research and older media can also have their own legacy storage locations; use the Docs drawer and a full profile backup to include them.

Backups (see **Backup, restore, auto-update**) include all of these.

## Deleting

Use the trash icon on a file you own, or select several files and choose
**Delete selected**. Deletion removes the files and their saved version history;
deleted code projects lose all their files. Files shared with you can be
downloaded but only their owner can delete them.
